title: Agnes Martin — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Agnes Martin's rich face, its first round, a Sketch and still a proposal: one walk, from one hand-ruled line beside a true one to a blind test of the page's perceptual claim that a grid held still makes a hair of drift visible and that without it the drift vanishes into noise. Every line on it is drawn by the piece from a stated model of a hand; nothing of hers is reproduced and nothing is quoted beyond the page. The dossier stays in the bundle and off the face: it carries quotations the page does not, marked to be verified. I grow when the page is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.
note: One piece, on the one section whose claim can be tested. The section's second paragraph ('I receive' against what she destroyed) is a claim about a person, with nothing a piece can test, and is left to the text. The record's gathered dossier is not shown: it quotes beyond the page, and the person-page rule here is no quotation beyond what the page carries.

offers.what: The sentence 'take it away and the difference vanishes into noise' is a claim about seeing, stated as fact in the narrator's voice; the intro frames the grid idea as 'her account of it', this paragraph does not. Offer: let the paragraph keep the claim as hers ('to her, the grid holds still so…') or say plainly that it is a perceptual claim a reader can test (the rich face's piece does). Making the piece also showed what 'take the grid away' has to mean to be testable: remove the even spacing, the shared edge and the cross-rules while the lines themselves stay the same; one clause could say so. No reader has taken the test yet, so nothing here says the claim is right or wrong.

pieces.title: the grid holds still · a walk in five steps
pieces.caption: **Can you see the hand drift?** One hand-ruled line beside a true one; the hand's drift stated as a rule (a smoothed random walk pinned at both ends, scaled to *a* px root mean square); ten lines held in a grid; the same ten, line for line, with the grid taken away; then 64 blind fields, straight or drifting by a fair coin, at four amplitudes, with the grid and without. Chance and the verdict rule are stated before the first field, both halves are scored, and the piece reads its own pixels to show the two halves differ only in the grid. All lines are original; nothing of hers is reproduced. The threshold that answers the page is the reader's.
